newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian skydivers survive 500 metre fall.
newsitem.headline: Australian skydivers survive 500 metre fall.

text.p: Two Australian skydivers survived a 500 metre (1,640 feet) fall to the ground after they collided in mid-air, a national skydiving official said on Wednesday.

Hundreds of horrified spectators at the National Skydiving Championships at Corowa, 540 km (335 miles) southwest of Sydney, watched as the two skydivers' parachutes became entangled and they crashed into a paddock.
Geoff Divco was taken to hospital with a fractured skull, a collapsed lung and broken ribs. His jumping partner, Jerome Rich, escaped with minor bruisesg.
The pair decided to make a non-competition jump with a small group of skydivers at about 7.00 p.m. (0800GMT) on Tuesday, said Gary Myors, safety officer at the championships.
The pair jumped from the aircraft at about 4,000 metres (13,000 feet) and completed a free-fall routine, but became entangled when they opened their parachutes, Myors told Reuters.
"Basically they just ran into each other. Their parachutes opened, but when they collided the parachutes collapsed and they crashed into the paddock," he said.
